# Switchboard — Webhook Delivery Service

> **Purpose.** Switchboard turns internal domain events into outbound **webhooks**:
> a team publishes an event once, and Switchboard delivers it as a signed HTTP
> request to every endpoint subscribed to that event type.

**Scope:** v2 only — the queue-backed delivery workers. The legacy v1 synchronous
path is out of scope.

## 1. Architecture

An event is accepted, queued, and delivered by a worker pool. Nothing is delivered
in the publisher's request path, so a slow subscriber can never slow a publisher.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Internal services] -->|publish| B[Ingest API]
  B --> Q[(events queue)]
  Q --> W[Delivery workers]
  W -->|signed POST| S[Subscriber endpoints]
  W -.retry.-> R[(retry queue)]
  R -.exhausted.-> D[(dead letter)]
```

## 2. Delivery guarantees

| Guarantee | What it means | Where it is enforced |
|-----------|---------------|----------------------|
| At least once | Every accepted event is delivered one or more times | Retry queue |
| Ordered per subscriber | Events for one endpoint keep publish order | Partition key |
| Signed | Each request carries an HMAC of its body | Delivery worker |

> **Note.** At-least-once means a subscriber **can** see a duplicate. Endpoints must
> be idempotent — key on the `Event-Id` header.

## 3. Retry policy

Failures back off exponentially, then land in the dead-letter queue.

- [x] Exponential backoff, jittered
- [x] Dead-letter after 12 attempts
- [ ] Per-subscriber circuit breaker

```sh
# replay a dead-lettered event
switchboard replay --event 01J9Z8...
```
